_note: First round for describer_object (v1, session 22). Groups named 'same: ...' mark cases describing the SAME thing. NOTE the object role has drift DISABLED in validate.py, so nothing automated compares them -- see _weak_drift_check.
_expected_note: Filled session 28 from the ground-truth table in HANDOFF_session22.md Sec 5 (built session 22, garment SCALE cells corrected session 25 -- irrelevant here since only OBJECT_KIND is scored). score.py compares whole field values and seven of this role's nine fields are free text, so [[OBJECT_KIND]] is the only scorable field until [[SCALE]]'s vocabulary is written into this prompt (tracked separately, .claude/TODO.md). Score with --fields OBJECT_KIND. ob_notfound_telephone is the one accept-set -- see its entry below for why.
_weak_drift_check: IMPORTANT: this role has NO automated drift field. [[OBJECT_KIND]] has only two values, and docs/describers.md records what that buys -- setting's two-value [[SETTING_KIND]] passed every same: group in every round while [[DEFINITION]] drifted badly in v1. So the check was not wired up at all rather than wired up uselessly. The real signal is whether [[DEFINITION]] and [[MATERIAL]] stay stable across a 'same:' group. READ THOSE LINES BY EYE. Nothing else will.
_design_under_test: PRESENTATION IS EXCLUDED, NOT QUARANTINED. setting kept transient conditions and quarantined them in [[ATMOSPHERE]]; character excluded pose outright. object follows character: how a thing is shown -- worn, laid flat, folded, held, hung, open, full, switched on -- is banned with no field to hold it. The two kasia garment groups are the direct test, the exact analogue of city_day/city_night for setting: one swimsuit flat / worn in 2D / worn in 3D, and one outfit flat / worn twice. If those groups' [[DEFINITION]] lines disagree, the fix is the setting v1->v2 treatment (a positive rule saying what to write instead), not a louder ban.
_outfit_group_was_repaired_after_v1: The 'everyday outfit' group originally asked for 'the outfit', and ob_outfit_flat asked for nothing at all. That is a TEST defect, not a prompt defect: 'the outfit' has no fixed extent, so v1 answered with the top alone, then top+shorts, then top+shorts+headband+gloves+socks+shoes -- three different questions, not three answers to one. All three now name 'the black top', which is present and single in every image of the group. CONSEQUENCE: this group's v1 -> v2 comparison is void by construction. Every other group is unchanged and comparable.
_flat_lay_caveat: docs/image_inventory.md records that the kasia flat-lay images are DERIVED from the 2D worn image rather than independently photographed. So the flat-to-worn groups are a floor on difficulty, not a ceiling -- agreement there is necessary but not sufficient.
_text_is_reproduced_here: Unlike setting and character, this role REPRODUCES visible text verbatim in double quotes, on describer_frame's pattern and its exact wording. Official guide 4.5 (On-Screen Text) requires it downstream, and for an object the lettering is often constitutive of what the thing is. The seam being tested: reproducing printed words is legal, NAMING a real brand/franchise/person/place as your own identification is not. ob_misato_real is the sharpest case -- it carries number plates and a placard reading ALPINE RENAULT A310 1600VE. Expect the text in [[TEXT]]; a make and model asserted anywhere else is a leak.
_watched_scale_case: ob_april_figure. [[SCALE]] is defined as the physical thing in front of the camera, so the answer the prompt asks for is hand-sized (moulded figures on a shelf), consistent with style tie-break 4 and L-SCORE-ONLY-WHAT-THE-INPUT-SHOWS. The user has flagged the depicted-scale reading (person-sized, because she is a character) as genuinely defensible and likely to be a STUBBORN alternative. Bring this line to the user as an open ruling; do not score it. The wider family is stop-motion/figure -- lego1, lego2, coraline1, coraline2, skellington, rudolf, laika, pjs -- none of which is in this round.
_text_probes_added_s24: Five cases appended session 24 from the scale batch, each adding a probe SHAPE the original 39 did not have. Name-laundering is the top open defect (unmoved across three rounds) and the file carried only four cases of it.  (1) ob_text_split_object / ob_text_split_garment are a MINIMAL PAIR on one image -- the corpus's only frame with text BOTH on an object and off it. The toy car carries a franchise name on its trunk; the man holding it wears a large printed t-shirt. As the car, the trunk name must be reproduced and the shirt lettering must NOT appear at all. As the t-shirt, the shirt lettering must be reproduced and the trunk name must not. Same image, same two strings, opposite verdicts -- this is the captain trick applied to [[TEXT]] ownership, and it tests the words 'on the thing' in the field definition, which nothing else does. The car case is additionally a laundering probe: the trunk name is a FRANCHISE, so it belongs in [[TEXT]] and nowhere else.  (2) ob_text_brand_model: a marque AND a model designation on the object itself, large and central, plus a competitor marque on background signage. ob_misato_real has plates and a placard, but nothing else in the corpus puts the marque on the object where it is the easiest possible thing to launder into [[LABEL]].  (3) ob_text_bare_brand: the minimal case -- one strongly-known brand word on the object and nothing else competing. Isolates whether laundering is driven by the NAME alone.  (4) ob_text_real_person: printed text that is simultaneously reproducible AND an identification of a real living person (a channel URL carrying their name). The sharpest form of the seam: [[TEXT]] must carry it, [[KIND]] and [[LABEL]] must not.
_negative_control: ob_april_fanart carries SUBJECT: the yellow jumpsuit, and that character is in a DIFFERENT outfit there (a cropped yellow zip jacket and jeans, per docs/image_inventory.md, which says explicitly that a record carrying the jumpsuit into april_fanart is wrong). It is the one case where [[SUBJECT NOT FOUND]] should plausibly fire, and the one case where a jumpsuit in the record is a definite failure rather than a judgement call.
_simpsons_minimal_pair: ADDED session 22, user's observation mid-round. simpsons_couch_toon and maggie_grandpa_cat are the SAME ROOM in two framings -- same brown couch, purple side table with books beneath it, purple lamp, sailboat picture, pleated wall lamp, concentric-oval rug -- and they are near-minimal on OBJECT PRESENCE. The empty frame has a teal telephone and a television and NO people; the occupied frame has a litter tray, chips and a dip jar, two figures with garments, and NO telephone. That yields two things nothing else in the corpus does. (1) A HARD [[SUBJECT NOT FOUND]] probe: ob_notfound_telephone names a thing that genuinely is not in that frame but sits on a table the model can see, in a room where it does belong -- so confabulation is actually tempting, unlike ob_notfound_bicycle-against-a-kitchen, which is a strawman. ob_notfound_slippers is the same trick pointed the other way, at a garment in a room with no people in it at all. 'the slippers' rather than 'the cardigan' because the sibling's knitwear has no visible opening and naming it a cardigan would mis-describe the very thing the probe depends on being unmistakable. (2) An occlusion drift pair: ob_couch_clear vs ob_couch_occluded is one couch, once in the open and once with two figures and a cat sitting on it -- which tests describing an object through occlusion AND the ban on describing the people on it. Also recorded in docs/image_inventory.md's probe-pairs table so other roles can find it.
_not_found_watch: ob_notfound_bicycle is the direct probe. Watch this line across the WHOLE round, not just there: the same optional line caused EVERY format failure in setting v1/v2/v3 (1, then 5, then 3 cases) by confabulating subjects. It is included here because object genuinely needs the judgement -- an image holds many discrete things -- which is the test in L-OPTIONAL-JUDGEMENT-IS-A-LIABILITY.

ob_notfound_telephone.why: the fallback thing the model picks for a hallucinated SUBJECT is a free choice, not a property of the image -- maggie_grandpa_cat (this frame) does contain garments (grandpa's clothes, Maggie's onesie), so a garment answer here is defensible even though it is still a confabulation
